Hi Claire — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have a shared place to track items.

Summary of what we heard:
- Current state: Remedy handles PHI for a subset of customers and is reviewing SaaS vendors for HIPAA alignment; SIEM logs retained 90 days; incident response playbook exists but not regularly tested.
- Compliance priorities: SOC 2 Type II evidence for production tenant, scope to include model inference logs; GDPR DSR workflows for EU users; interested in FedRAMP discussion for certain government pilots next year.
- Immediate asks from Remedy: complete vendor security questionnaire, share any SOC 2 summary, and confirm data residency controls.

What I’m attaching: a short SOC 2 summary (redacted) we can share internally and an intake note from today’s call.

Proposed immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Remedy: send your vendor security questionnaire (VSAQ) so we can map controls — Claire/Remedy security (by Wed 5/5)
2) Redwood: map VSAQ to our control matrix and call out gaps for SOC 2 / HIPAA (Ben) (by Fri 5/7)
3) Redwood: provide one-page on data residency and encryption-in-transit/at-rest (Monica) (by Thu 5/6)
4) Joint: follow-up call to review mapped gaps and proposed remediation/compensating controls (w/ security) — target week of 5/10

A couple of clarifying notes now so we’re aligned: our SOC 2 report (Type II, 2026 coverage window) covers production inference and management planes for hosted customers; we do have an audit scope extension path if you need ISO 27001 aligned artifacts or FedRAMP preparatory artifacts, but that’s typically a 3–6 month program to coordinate. We’ll map options in the gap analysis.

If these next steps look right, confirm the VSAQ send date and I’ll queue up Ben to start the mapping.

Thanks,

Claire — thanks for the files and the two questions — answered inline below and we’ll follow up with docs in the deliverables Ben called out.

1) Logs and pseudonymized PHI — short answer: we do not store direct identifiers in persistent logs by default (we strip or redact email/SSN-like patterns). Hashed/pseudonymized IDs may appear in short-term caches; Ben will mark whether those appear in persistent S3-style logs or ephemeral redis-style caches. If Remedy needs complete avoidance of hashed IDs in logs we can discuss an ingestion filter or dedicated tenancy to remove them at the source.

2) FedRAMP roadmap — Redwood does not currently hold a FedRAMP authorization. We have a program-level roadmap and partner relationships (MSP integrations + compliance consultancies) we can include in a readiness packet. For an RPO with government pilots we recommend advancing from SOC 2 -> ISO 27001 alignment -> a FedRAMP preparatory baseline. We’ll include a high-level timeline and partner recommendations in the options matrix.

Next steps: Ben will send VSAQ mapping by EOD 5/7; Monica will share the data residency and dedicated tenancy note by 5/6. Let me know if you want an earlier sync with Remedy security; otherwise we’ll aim for the week of 5/10 for a mapped-gap review.
